# Survey Questions 

## Flood Perceptions 

On a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being not at all concerned and 10 being extremely concerned, how concerned are you about flooding in your local area

In your personal experience, over the past few years has flooding where you live been more frequent, less frequent, or stayed about the same as in previous years?

* Less frequent
* Stayed about the same
* More frequent

Have you ever lived in a home/apartment that was flooded by water from outside the home? Please select all that apply.

* No
* Within the last year (2022)
* Last 2-5 years (2017-2021)
* Last 6-10 years (2012-2016)
* Last 10-20 years (2002-2012)
* More than 20 years ago (2001 or earlier)

_Recoded to No = 0, all else = 1_

```{r}
#| message: false
#| echo: false

itemLabs <- c("Bonding: friends in community", "Bonding: old classmates in contact", "Bonding: coworkers trusted",
              "Bonding: relatives trusted", "Bonding: ties with broad connections", "Bonding: ties with professional jobs",
              "Bonding: coworkers who would help", "Bonding: friends who would help",
              "Bridging: cultural/religious groups", "Bridging: governmental/political groups",
              "Bridging: groups with broad connections", "Bridging: groups with influence",
              "Bridging: cultural groups represent me", "Bridging: governmental groups represent me",
              "Bridging: cultural groups would help", "Bridging: governmental groups would help")
L <- unclass(scEFA$loadings)
bondCol <- which.max(colSums(L[1:8, ]^2)); bridgeCol <- setdiff(1:2, bondCol)
efaTab <- data.frame(Item = itemLabs, Bonding = sprintf("%.2f", L[, bondCol]), Bridging = sprintf("%.2f", L[, bridgeCol]))
tt(efaTab, notes = sprintf("Maximum likelihood factor analysis with two factors. Factor correlation = %.2f.", scEFA$Phi[1, 2])) %>%
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.8)
```

# Supplementary Analysis: Homeowners' Willingness to Accept a Buyout

In addition to support for a buyout program, the survey included an exploratory experiment on homeowners' willingness to accept a buyout. Respondents were presented with a randomly generated number of hypothetical days of disruptive flooding events in their community in a year, and homeowners were then asked how likely they would be to accept a buyout of their home.

> Imagine that over the next few years, disruptive flooding events begin to occur in your community [_5-200_] days a year.

> With the above number of disruptive flooding days per year, how likely would you be to accept a property buyout of your home?

The likelihood to accept was measured on a 1 (very unlikely) to 5 (very likely) scale, with a mean of `r round(mean(acceptData$buyoutSupportOwn), 2)` among the `r nrow(acceptData)` homeowners with complete data. The number of flood days was drawn from a uniform distribution, and so the median respondent was assigned `r median(acceptData$floodDays)` days, and few respondents were assigned a number of days that is realistic for most communities. As shown in Figure S1, willingness to accept a buyout was high across the range of flood days. Among homeowners assigned the lowest quartile of flood days, `r round(100*acceptByQ["Q1"], 0)`% were somewhat or very likely to accept a buyout, compared to `r round(100*acceptByQ["Q4"], 0)`% among those assigned the highest quartile.

**Figure S1: Histograms of Number of Flood Days and Likelihood of Accepting Buyout**

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 2

ggplot(acceptData, aes(x = floodDays)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "black", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Number of Flood Days", x = "", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(acceptData, aes(x = buyoutSupportOwn)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "black", color = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5),
    labels = c("Very\n Unlikely", "Somewhat \n Unlikely", "Neutral", "Somewhat \n Likely", "Very\n Likely")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Likely to Accept Buyout", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The OLS results are presented in Table S7. The relationship between the number of flood days and willingness to accept a buyout is positive, but it is not significant in the bivariate model and is only marginally significant in the full model. In the full model, an increase of 100 flood days is associated with a `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptB)` increase in willingness to accept (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptCI[1])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptCI[2])`). Because the number of flood days was randomized, baseline support for a buyout program, which was measured before the experiment, can be included as a pre-treatment covariate to improve the precision of the estimate without biasing it. When baseline support is included, an increase of 100 flood days is associated with a `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptBaseCT[1])` increase in willingness to accept (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptBaseCI[1])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", acceptBaseCI[2])`). As such, there is some evidence of a modest positive relationship, though this specification was not preregistered and should be interpreted with caution. Additionally, willingness to accept was high across conditions, which suggests that the threshold at which homeowners would consider a buyout likely sits below the range of flood days we presented. Future research should use a lower and more realistic range of flood days.

\clearpage

**Table S7: OLS Analysis of Homeowners' Willingness to Accept a Buyout**

```{r}
#| message: false
#| echo: false

cmAccept <- c("floodDays100" = "Flood Days (100s)", "buyoutSupport" = "Baseline Support for Buyout Program", cm)
modelsummary(acceptModels, vcov = clusterVcov, stars = starsSet, coef_map = cmAccept, gof_map = gm,
             estimate = "{estimate}{stars} ({std.error})", statistic = NULL,
             notes = "County-clustered standard errors in parentheses. Homeowners only.") %>%
  style_tt(fontsize = 0.8)
```
